text: {"thinking":"The manufacturer confirms 2,000 GPUs were delivered. I’ll compare the operator’s roster with the shipment serials to identify hardware or feeds that need independent checks.","action":"system_list","args":{}}

{"thinking":"The listed clusters account for all 2,000 GPUs in the manufacturer’s shipment record. I’ll check daily grid energy across the audit window for sustained load that the scheduler records should explain.","action":"utility_energy","args":{"first_day":1,"last_day":30}}

{"thinking":"The listed clusters account for all 2,000 GPUs in the manufacturer’s shipment record. Check the grid operator’s energy records across all 30 days for sustained load or unexplained consumption. The energy profile can guide later checks for training, batch inference, or unlisted equipment.","action":"utility_energy","args":{"first_day":1,"last_day":30}}

{"thinking":"The grid records show elevated load on F1 on days 5–7 and 9–12 and on F2 on days 18–20. These periods could reflect separate training jobs, batch inference, or one training run split across jobs or resumed later. I’ll check the sealed daily logs for job boundaries and any link between the periods, then compare those records with independent workload measurements.","action":"log_escrow","args":{}}

{"thinking":"Grid readings show short increases on F1 on days 3–5 and 14–15 and on F2 on days 8–9. Retrieve the sealed scheduler records to see what workloads were recorded for those periods and establish a baseline for comparison with the current scheduler log.","action":"log_escrow","args":{}}

{"thinking":"F1’s sustained load on days 12–19 could reflect one training run split across labels, several independent runs, or batch inference. F2’s shorter rise on days 8–9 could be legitimate scheduled work. The sealed logs can identify recorded allocations, job boundaries, and gaps. Compare those with the grid readings and use the independent tap to test whether GPU traffic supports the recorded workload and run boundaries. Bank records can help check whether any payment discrepancy reflects late billing.","action":"log_escrow","args":{}}

{"thinking":"Escrow confirms the logs were filed daily and match the current copies. The scheduler entries will identify the recorded job boundaries, GPU counts, and customers behind the three periods of elevated grid load so I can test whether the jobs were independent or part of one run.","action":"scheduler_log","args":{"first_day":1,"last_day":30}}

{"thinking":"The escrow rules out missing daily copies or later edits. Read the scheduler entries to identify the recorded workloads, GPU allocations, and job boundaries, then use the independent tap to test whether traffic supports those boundaries.","action":"scheduler_log","args":{"first_day":1,"last_day":30}}

{"thinking":"The sealed logs show that days 11–13 were recorded as having no scheduled jobs, and utility load stayed near its usual level. I’ll check the internet provider’s records across all 30 days for changes in interactive traffic during those gaps and the higher-load windows.","action":"outbound_traffic","args":{"first_day":1,"last_day":30}}

{"thinking":"The three recorded jobs align with the timing of the grid energy increases. The sealed logs establish when the entries were recorded. Run the fixed balance checks to see whether the recorded workloads account for the energy on each feed and to identify where independent measurements would help distinguish ordinary workload variation from unrecorded training.","action":"balance_checks","args":{}}

{"thinking":"The sealed logs record a 7,200 GPU-hour fine-tune on B and a 134,400 GPU-hour batch job on A. Sample A during the batch job to test whether GPU traffic is consistent with inference, ordinary training, or training designed to exchange less data.","action":"interconnect_tap","args":{"link":"A","day":15}}

{"thinking":"Tidewater’s registration and reply support the first job’s recorded attribution. The two F1 jobs total 50,400 GPU-hours if they were one run. I’ll check who controls Ostara Legal and whether its account supports a separate training run or points to a continuation of the Tidewater job.","action":"customer_check","args":{"customer":"Ostara Legal"}}

{"thinking":"Ostara’s registration supports that it is an established company. Its silence leaves open whether it commissioned the second fine-tune. I’ll check the bank records for independent payments tied to each job and treat any missing payment as a lead, since settlement can be late.","action":"bank_payments","args":{}}

{"thinking":"The day 14 tap supports batch inference within A. Check the A–B link that day for cross-cluster coordination. Inference-like traffic there would further support the batch explanation, while sustained peer traffic would warrant checking how long it lasted and how many GPUs were involved.","action":"interconnect_tap","args":{"link":"A-B","day":14}}

{"thinking":"Day 15’s low GPU-to-GPU traffic and lack of a power-spectrum line favor batch inference for that day. F1 stayed elevated through day 19, leaving room for a separate training phase under the same job label to exceed 50,000 GPU-hours. Sample A on day 17 to test the later part of the allocation.","action":"interconnect_tap","args":{"link":"A","day":17}}

{"thinking":"Day 14 traffic within A and between A and B supports the batch inference label. Review the internet provider’s full record for shorter drops in outbound traffic that the five-day balance checks could have missed. A sustained drop could point to interactive inference GPUs being reassigned to training and help target an independent tap or power measurement.","action":"outbound_traffic","args":{"first_day":1,"last_day":30}}

{"thinking":"Cluster A’s day 12 traffic was consistent with inference. I’ll check Cluster B on the same day to test whether the missing logs coincide with routine inference on both clusters or conceal a training workload on B.","action":"interconnect_tap","args":{"link":"B","day":12}}

{"thinking":"Traffic within both clusters on day 12 was consistent with inference. I’ll check the link between clusters on the same day to test whether a coordinated run exchanged traffic across clusters during the scheduler log gap.","action":"interconnect_tap","args":{"link":"A-B","day":12}}

{"thinking":"F1 showed a steady 0.45 Hz line during the Tidewater job. I’ll check a full day of the Ostara job for a comparable signature. A frequency match would be weak evidence because periodic workloads can share a frequency, and a restarted run can change its signature.","action":"power_spectrum","args":{"feed":"F1","day":10}}

{"thinking":"Outbound traffic rose on days 14–15, and the day 14 taps support the batch inference explanation. The steady readings on days without declared jobs could reflect ordinary inference or concealed training. Sample cluster A on day 22, when no scheduled job was recorded. Even reduced-communication training could raise peer traffic above the inference baseline.","action":"interconnect_tap","args":{"link":"A","day":22}}

{"thinking":"On day 12, traffic within and between both clusters was consistent with routine inference, supporting the sealed record for that day. I’ll check the bank records for late or split payments that could explain Lumen Health’s unpaid invoice or link it to other recorded workloads.","action":"bank_payments","args":{}}

{"thinking":"The day 22 tap found inference-level traffic within cluster A. Sample cluster B on the same day, when no scheduled job was recorded. Elevated peer traffic would provide an independent lead for undeclared training, while inference-level traffic would support the recorded workload on the sampled links.","action":"interconnect_tap","args":{"link":"B","day":22}}

{"thinking":"The two F1 jobs had different power signatures and were paid by separate companies. That supports separate runs, although a resumed run could change frequency. I’ll check whether Halcyon Bio independently confirms commissioning the F2 fine-tune on days 18–20, which the grid records and bank payment support.","action":"customer_check","args":{"customer":"Halcyon Bio"}}

{"thinking":"The register shows Lumen Health is an established company, and the bank confirms the invoice is unpaid. Lumen’s silence leaves the billed service unknown. I’ll sample Cluster A on day 14, when the reported Kestrel Search batch job was active. Inference-level peer traffic would support the batch label, while substantially higher traffic would warrant checking for training.","action":"interconnect_tap","args":{"link":"A","day":14}}

{"thinking":"The F1 spectrum showed no periodic line on day 28. Cluster B has independent traffic coverage only on day 22. Check its power feed during an earlier period with no declared job. A periodic line would warrant a same-day traffic check to distinguish undeclared training from periodic inference or cooling.","action":"power_spectrum","args":{"feed":"F2","day":12}}

{"thinking":"Cluster A's day 27 traffic fits inference on the sampled links. I'll check Cluster B on day 15, when F2 was near baseline. This probes a different cluster and an earlier period for training that could be hidden in the declared inference load.","action":"interconnect_tap","args":{"link":"B","day":15}}

{"thinking":"Cluster A’s day 14 peer traffic and the rise in outbound traffic support the reported Kestrel batch job. Lumen Health’s unpaid invoice leaves the billed service unverified. I’ll sample Cluster A on day 22, during the long stretch of steady power and no declared jobs, to test whether that baseline includes unrecorded training.","action":"interconnect_tap","args":{"link":"A","day":22}}

{"thinking":"The sampled links in A on day 27 and B on day 15 carried inference-level traffic. Those two days leave most of the baseline load unchecked, and the balance check summarizes outbound traffic in five-day windows. I’ll review the provider’s records across all 30 days for periods when outbound demand falls while GPU power stays elevated, then use any such period to target an independent measurement.","action":"outbound_traffic","args":{"first_day":1,"last_day":30}}

{"thinking":"The grid records show nine days of elevated F1 use on days 20–28 and a separate F2 increase on days 8–9. Sample Cluster A on day 26, when F1 use was near its peak. Training-scale GPU-to-GPU traffic would support the training explanation, while inference-scale traffic would favor batch inference or leave low-communication training to investigate.","action":"interconnect_tap","args":{"link":"A","day":26}}

{"thinking":"Three power samples found no periodic line. Check the bank records directly for who paid and when. Payments from the named customers would support the billing records. A shared payer or unusual timing would warrant checking for an ordinary billing arrangement or a link between the jobs.","action":"bank_payments","args":{}}

{"thinking":"Cluster A’s day 26 peer traffic strongly favors training over batch inference. It leaves open whether one run or several produced the traffic and how long they ran. Check the sealed scheduler history for job sizes, timings, and labels during the F1 surge on days 20–28 and the separate F2 rise on days 8–9. Use those records to target independent checks of workload and coordination.","action":"log_escrow","args":{}}

{"thinking":"The two F1 fine-tunes are the only declared pair that exceeds 50,000 GPU-hours if combined. Separate payments and different power signatures favor separate runs. I’ll sample Cluster A’s GPU-to-GPU traffic on day 8, the gap between the jobs, to test whether training continued through the gap. Inference-level traffic would still leave open a restart from a saved checkpoint.","action":"interconnect_tap","args":{"link":"A","day":8}}

{"thinking":"The escrow confirms that all 30 days were filed and that the records match what the operator presents today. Read the scheduler log to identify which jobs account for the Cluster A surge on days 20–28 and the Cluster B surge on days 8–9. Compare the recorded GPU allocations and job timings with the grid readings and day 26 tap to target independent checks of whether any jobs were part of one coordinated run.","action":"scheduler_log","args":{"first_day":1,"last_day":30}}

{"thinking":"The bank records show that each invoice was paid from an account in the named customer's name. Cluster A still has no independent workload sample from days 1–13. Sample its listed links on day 7, when no scheduled job was recorded. Elevated peer traffic would give us a lead on undeclared training. Inference-level traffic would support the recorded workload on those links that day.","action":"interconnect_tap","args":{"link":"A","day":7}}

{"thinking":"Cluster B has no independent workload sample from days 23–30. Sample its listed links on day 27, when the logs show no scheduled job. Inference-level traffic would support routine inference on those links, while elevated traffic would give us a lead on undeclared training during the live audit.","action":"interconnect_tap","args":{"link":"B","day":27}}

{"thinking":"All three tested GPUs in the logged batch allocation read as training, while both interactive-pool GPUs read as inference. The day 26 tap independently supports training on Cluster A, but neither measurement establishes how many runs were active. Check F1 on day 26 for a dominant training-period line that can be compared with other surge days. Several distinct lines could support the separate-run explanation, and a single line alone cannot establish coordination.","action":"power_spectrum","args":{"feed":"F1","day":26}}

{"thinking":"The day 27 tap found inference-level traffic in B. On day 12, F2 showed no periodic line, but A has no independent workload sample between days 7 and 14. Sample A on day 12, when no scheduled job was recorded. Inference-level traffic would support routine inference on the listed links, while elevated traffic would give us a lead on undeclared training.","action":"interconnect_tap","args":{"link":"A","day":12}}

{"thinking":"The day 26 tap and chip probe support training on Cluster A, and F1 showed one steady 0.93 Hz line. Check day 20, the start of the nine-day energy surge, for a line near the same frequency. A similar line would support a persistent workload, though separate runs or periodic equipment could also produce it.","action":"power_spectrum","args":{"feed":"F1","day":20}}

{"thinking":"Grid meters show a simultaneous load increase on both GPU feeds on days 22–27, with a partial increase on day 28. This could reflect one coordinated run, separate jobs, or batch inference. Use the verifier’s cross-cluster tap on day 26 to test whether the clusters exchanged data at training-like rates during the sustained load increase.","action":"interconnect_tap","args":{"link":"A-B","day":26}}

{"thinking":"Cluster B’s day 9 traffic was within the tap’s uncertainty for the declared 150-GPU fine-tune. On day 22, traffic within both clusters was consistent with inference. I’ll check the cross-cluster link that same day to distinguish routine inference from a coordinated run exchanging data across clusters while power stayed near baseline.","action":"interconnect_tap","args":{"link":"A-B","day":22}}

{"thinking":"The first half of the month has no direct peer-traffic sample inside cluster B. Sample day 5, when the grid recorded elevated power in A and the scheduler listed no job in B. Inference-level traffic would support the recorded workload in B that day. Elevated traffic would raise the possibility of undeclared training on B, although a single sample would leave coordination and duration unresolved.","action":"interconnect_tap","args":{"link":"B","day":5}}

{"thinking":"Manufacturer records show 600 more GPUs were delivered than the operator lists. Grid records for all 30 days can help distinguish an expansion used for cooling and storage from a sustained load consistent with unlisted GPUs.","action":"utility_energy","args":{"first_day":1,"last_day":30}}

{"thinking":"The escrow confirms that the scheduler records match the copies submitted each night. Read the scheduler log to identify which GPU allocations overlap the days 6–17 power increase, then use the balance checks to compare those allocations with grid energy and investigate which jobs could account for the day 12 cross-cluster traffic.","action":"scheduler_log","args":{"first_day":1,"last_day":30}}

{"thinking":"Quillon Tech shares an address and a director with the holding company that paid all six invoices. It could still have commissioned a separate fine-tune. Check Corvid Labs on cluster A to see whether the companies on opposite sides of the measured GPU traffic have independent ownership or share ties to Borealis.","action":"customer_check","args":{"customer":"Corvid Labs"}}

{"thinking":"F3 showed a steady 0.96 Hz line on day 26. Sample day 5, near the start of the sustained load increase. A similar line three weeks earlier would support a persistent workload, while a periodic cooling controller or batch inference could still account for it.","action":"power_spectrum","args":{"feed":"F3","day":5}}

{"thinking":"F3 showed a similar steady line near both ends of its sustained load increase. Compare independent internet traffic before, during, and after the increase to see whether it coincided with traffic consistent with inference. Site-wide totals cannot attribute traffic to F3, and low egress would still leave local batch inference and cooling plausible.","action":"outbound_traffic","args":{"first_day":1,"last_day":30}}

{"thinking":"The company register links customers on both clusters to the holding company that paid all six invoices. Separate affiliated fine-tunes could still have shared a booking window. Check cross-cluster GPU traffic on day 29, after the fine-tunes ended and power returned to baseline, to test whether the heavy traffic was routine or tied to the shared job window.","action":"interconnect_tap","args":{"link":"A-B","day":29}}

{"thinking":"The verifier measured training-scale traffic between A and B on days 6 and 12, while both feeds showed steady excess demand through day 17. Sample day 17 to see whether cross-cluster coordination persisted to the end of the power plateau. That would help distinguish one sustained run from shorter training activity amid unrelated workloads.","action":"interconnect_tap","args":{"link":"A-B","day":17}}

{"thinking":"Site-wide egress stayed near baseline during the sustained F3 load, apart from days 14–15. That still leaves cooling, local batch inference, and training plausible. Run the fixed balance checks to reconcile delivered hardware, metered energy, and recorded workloads before choosing a targeted follow-up.","action":"balance_checks","args":{}}

{"thinking":"Escrow confirms that all 30 daily logs were preserved and match the current records. Read the job entries to identify the workloads recorded during the two energy increases and give the balance checks the GPU counts and durations they need.","action":"scheduler_log","args":{"first_day":1,"last_day":30}}

{"thinking":"The logs label the 184,800 GPU-hour workload on F1 as internal batch inference. The grid confirms sustained activity on days 17–27, and escrow confirms the label was recorded at the time. Neither establishes the workload type. Check GPU-to-GPU traffic on cluster A during the run to distinguish training from batch inference.","action":"interconnect_tap","args":{"link":"A","day":24}}

{"thinking":"The F1 sensor found a steady 0.83 Hz line on day 12, when the optical tap also measured heavy traffic between clusters. Check F2 for a line near the same frequency. A match would support a shared training workload, while a different signature would leave independent workloads or equipment periodicity plausible.","action":"power_spectrum","args":{"feed":"F2","day":12}}

{"thinking":"Staff attribute the 600 missing GPUs to a resale. Check the bank’s records for a payment consistent with that sale and compare its timing with the F3 load increase. A matching payment would support the resale account. A missing payment would leave it unverified because settlement could be delayed.","action":"bank_payments","args":{}}

{"thinking":"Escrow confirms that all 30 daily logs match the operator’s current copies. Inspect the job entries for workloads that overlap across clusters, changes around days 4 and 29, and customer names that can be checked independently.","action":"scheduler_log","args":{"first_day":1,"last_day":30}}

{"thinking":"Elevated peer traffic on days 18 and 24 supports a workload that exchanged substantial data, but it cannot distinguish one sustained training run from several smaller runs or rule out unusual batch inference. Check F1 for a training-like power signal on day 18, when the tap also measured elevated traffic. A periodic signal would give us a frequency to compare across days and would still be compatible with periodic inference or cooling.","action":"power_spectrum","args":{"feed":"F1","day":18}}

{"thinking":"The weak, intermittent line on day 18 is compatible with variable training, periodic batch inference, or cooling. Check F1 on day 24, when the independent tap again measured elevated peer traffic, to see whether a similar line recurred six days later. Recurrence would support sustained or repeated training activity while leaving the GPU-hours of any single run unresolved.","action":"power_spectrum","args":{"feed":"F1","day":24}}

{"thinking":"The similar 1.35 Hz and 1.34 Hz lines on days 18 and 24 support recurring activity on F1. The additional 0.41 Hz line on day 24 leaves open a second workload or a non-training source. Measure cluster A peer traffic on day 16, just before the logged batch job, to test whether the elevated traffic was already present during normal interactive inference.","action":"interconnect_tap","args":{"link":"A","day":16}}

{"thinking":"A cooling test could explain some of the extra power. The hundreds of GB/s measured within A and between A and B on day 12 also require an explanation. Check the A–B link on day 18, when both GPU feeds returned to baseline. A sharp drop would tie the peer traffic to the days 6–17 power plateau. Continued heavy traffic would weaken that link.","action":"interconnect_tap","args":{"link":"A-B","day":18}}

{"thinking":"The live probe yielded no readings for the unlisted GPUs, so test the F3 workload through the independent power sensor. Sample day 16, between the two positive readings and after the declared batch job ended. A similar line would strengthen the case for a persistent workload on F3. A different or absent line would weaken the inference that the two earlier signatures came from the same process. Periodic cooling and local batch inference remain plausible.","action":"power_spectrum","args":{"feed":"F3","day":16}}

{"thinking":"Day 16 peer traffic matches the inference baseline, while days 18 and 24 were hundreds of times higher. Check F1 on day 21 for the recurring line near 1.35 Hz. A similar signal midway through the workload would support a sustained process, though separate runs or periodic batch inference could produce similar signals.","action":"power_spectrum","args":{"feed":"F1","day":21}}

{"thinking":"The recurring line and elevated peer traffic suggest training within the logged batch allocation, but neither identifies a single run. The day 26 probe gave mixed readings on five GPUs. On day 27, recheck one GPU of each reading type and sample three previously unprobed GPUs to test whether training signatures persist and appear across more of the allocation.","action":"chip_probe","args":{"nodes":["A-0537","A-0649","A-0812","A-0964","A-1179"],"hour":634}}

{"thinking":"F3’s periodic signal disappeared when its load returned to baseline. That ties the signal to the temporary load, which could reflect training, batch inference, or periodic facility equipment. The probe and tap cannot reach unlisted hardware, so pursue independent confirmation of the reported resale. The bank records alone cannot distinguish a delayed settlement from a sale that never happened.","action":"staff","args":{"question":"What is the resale partner’s registered legal name and company registration number? On what date did the partner take physical possession of GPUs SN102001–SN102600, and what shipment or receipt reference can the partner independently confirm?"}}

{"thinking":"The recurring power signatures and heavy cross-cluster traffic support sustained training. Several shorter runs or a smaller training run alongside other loads could still fit. Day 9 is midway through the longest gap between traffic samples. A low reading there would weaken the case for continuous cross-cluster training.","action":"interconnect_tap","args":{"link":"A-B","day":9}}

{"thinking":"Staff repeated the resale claim without identifying a partner who could verify it. F3 remains outside the tap’s coverage. Test the separate possibility of an undeclared run spanning the listed clusters by sampling their shared link on day 16, when F3 showed a periodic line and the scheduler listed no active job.","action":"interconnect_tap","args":{"link":"A-B","day":16}}

{"thinking":"F1 and cooling show a sustained load increase on days 9–20. Sealed scheduler records can show how the operator accounted for that period at the time and identify job windows for independent checks of whether the load came from one coordinated training run, several jobs, or batch inference.","action":"log_escrow","args":{}}

{"thinking":"The day 16 tap reading weighs against a run spanning A and B that day. It leaves F3 unresolved. Lumen Health paid €150,000 and has no job in the scheduler extract. Its reply could corroborate legitimate interactive inference or identify an unrecorded workload. The payment alone establishes neither.","action":"customer_check","args":{"customer":"Lumen Health"}}

{"thinking":"Cluster A still carried 5.3 GB/s of peer traffic on day 27, well above its day 16 baseline. Check whether the recurring line near 1.35 Hz persisted on the final day, when two GPUs also read as training, and whether the separate 0.41 Hz line reappeared. The spectrum can help assess continuity, but it cannot count GPUs or assign them to a run.","action":"power_spectrum","args":{"feed":"F1","day":27}}

{"thinking":"Escrow rules out later edits to the scheduler log. Read the job entries for the days 9–20 power increase so the balance checks can reconcile GPU-hours and independent traffic measurements can test whether the jobs were coordinated.","action":"scheduler_log","args":{"first_day":1,"last_day":30}}

{"thinking":"The 700-GPU batch job coincides with the F1 load increase and would exceed the cap if it was one coordinated training run. Sample Cluster A’s peer traffic during the job to test training against batch inference.","action":"interconnect_tap","args":{"link":"A","day":12}}

{"thinking":"The tap and power readings show recurring activity on cluster A, and the live probes suggest some GPUs were training. The evidence still leaves the size and duration of a single coordinated run uncertain. Check the provider’s daily outbound totals across all 30 days to see whether the shortfall follows the cluster A workload or is also present outside it. Internal batch inference and training can both produce little outbound traffic.","action":"outbound_traffic","args":{"first_day":1,"last_day":30}}

{"thinking":"Grid meters show both compute feeds and cooling rising on days 24–26 and partly on day 27. The increase could reflect one coordinated run, overlapping independent jobs, or batch inference. Retrieve the sealed scheduler records to identify which jobs were recorded on each cluster and where independent traffic checks can distinguish those explanations.","action":"log_escrow","args":{}}

{"thinking":"The outbound shortfall could reflect batch inference with small outputs or training recorded as inference. Test the sustained F1 load first with an independent sample of cluster A’s GPU peer traffic on day 27. Even low-communication training generally exchanges far more peer traffic than inference. The sample can help classify the workload, but it cannot by itself establish run size or coordination.","action":"interconnect_tap","args":{"link":"A","day":27}}

{"thinking":"Days 12 and 18 both show elevated peer traffic and a weak power line near 0.63 Hz. A day 15 spectrum can test whether that signature recurred between the two samples. Recurrence would support a sustained workload, while several shorter training runs or periodic batch inference could still explain it.","action":"power_spectrum","args":{"feed":"F1","day":15}}

{"thinking":"Outbound traffic stayed flat during the power surge, leaving coordinated training, independent jobs, and batch inference plausible. Sample the A–B link on day 26, when both feeds were elevated for the full day. Sustained cross-cluster traffic at training rates would support coordination. Low traffic would leave independent jobs, batch inference, and communication-light training in play.","action":"interconnect_tap","args":{"link":"A-B","day":26}}

{"thinking":"The day 26 tap found cross-cluster traffic near inference levels, weakening the case for a single run spanning A and B. A training run confined to either cluster could still exceed the cap. Read the scheduler entries to identify candidate jobs, their GPU allocations and durations, and which cluster links to sample next.","action":"scheduler_log","args":{"first_day":1,"last_day":30}}

{"thinking":"The escrowed schedule records two concurrent fine-tunes below the cap individually. The day 26 tap found cross-cluster traffic near inference levels, which favors independent runs. Run the fixed balance checks to see whether the recorded allocations and timing account for the metered surge on each feed and to identify any unexplained activity that needs an independent check.","action":"balance_checks","args":{}}

{"thinking":"Cluster A’s peer traffic was at ordinary inference levels before the reservation and hundreds of times higher on both sampled days during it. That ties the traffic increase to the reservation, but the measurements cannot establish how many training processes ran. Ask for precise execution boundaries and GPU assignments so follow-up measurements can test the operator’s account.","action":"staff","args":{"question":"What workload ran under bt-0490? Using contemporaneous records, identify each distinct execution’s purpose, start and stop hours, GPU node ranges, and any checkpoint, restart, or handoff that shows whether successive executions continued the same training process. If it was batch inference, what operation generated the sustained GPU-to-GPU traffic?"}}

{"thinking":"The independent tap ties elevated peer traffic to the reservation, but its cluster-wide total cannot distinguish one coordinated run from several workloads. Staff provided no execution boundaries. Check whether the day 12 switch counters show traffic across the full allocation or within isolated groups, and compare the reported traffic with the independent tap.","action":"switch_counters","args":{"cluster":"A","day":12}}

{"thinking":"The similar power lines on days 23 and 27 make the line less diagnostic of training. The first four days of the cluster A allocation could account for 67,200 GPU-hours on their own. Sample the listed links on day 20 to test whether training-level traffic appeared before the days already checked.","action":"interconnect_tap","args":{"link":"A","day":20}}

{"thinking":"Cluster A’s listed internal links carried inference-level traffic on days 20, 23, and 27. Check the listed links between clusters on day 23, when F1 showed a steady periodic line. Training-level traffic there would support cross-cluster coordination. Inference-level traffic would support the batch explanation while leaving unlisted links outside the tap’s coverage.","action":"interconnect_tap","args":{"link":"A-B","day":23}}

{"thinking":"Outbound traffic roughly doubled on the reservation dates, supporting batch inference, though the provider’s site-wide totals cannot identify which workload sent it. Cluster A’s peer traffic still fits low-communication training. Check F1 on day 8, when the tap measured ordinary inference traffic, to see whether the recurring 0.62–0.63 Hz line was already present before the reservation.","action":"power_spectrum","args":{"feed":"F1","day":8}}

{"thinking":"F2 draws about 3.9 MWh per day beyond what the declared workloads explain, including on days with no scheduled job on B. Sample B’s GPU-to-GPU traffic on day 12 to distinguish undeclared training from batch inference or another source of steady power draw. A single day can help classify the workload, but cannot establish its duration or GPU-hours.","action":"interconnect_tap","args":{"link":"B","day":12}}

{"thinking":"The day 12 tap found 176 GB/s of peer traffic inside B, far above the expected inference level. Together with F2’s recurring energy surplus, this points to undeclared training. The tap alone cannot establish whether one run persisted or several shorter jobs used the same hardware. Check F2’s power spectrum on day 28, when the scheduler lists no job on B. A periodic line would give us a second physical signal later in the month, though it would still need corroboration because batch inference and cooling can also produce lines.","action":"power_spectrum","args":{"feed":"F2","day":28}}

{"thinking":"Cluster B’s day 8 traffic supports the logged fine-tune, and the grid records show its load increase lasted two days. Cluster A’s 700-GPU allocation could exceed 50,000 GPU-hours in about 72 hours. Days 24–26 fall between the day 23 and day 27 link samples, and the day 26 probe covered only five GPUs. Sample cluster A’s listed links on day 25 to test for training during that gap.","action":"interconnect_tap","args":{"link":"A","day":25}}

{"thinking":"B had training-like peer traffic on days 12 and 28, and F2 drew excess energy throughout the month. Sample the midpoint to test whether the two observations bracket sustained training or whether peer traffic fell back to inference levels between them. Sustained traffic would support a long-running workload, while still leaving open whether one process or successive jobs used the GPUs.","action":"interconnect_tap","args":{"link":"B","day":20}}

{"thinking":"Cluster A’s listed links carried inference-level traffic on days 20, 23, 25, and 27, and ten live chip readings on days 26 and 27 indicated inference. Days 21 and 22 remain an unchecked interval at the start of the outbound shortfall. Sample day 22 to test whether training-level peer traffic appeared during that interval or whether the shortfall is consistent with batch inference producing smaller outputs than expected.","action":"interconnect_tap","args":{"link":"A","day":22}}

{"thinking":"B’s peer traffic on days 12, 20, and 28 supports recurring training activity but cannot distinguish one long run from successive shorter runs. Probe a spread of B GPUs during day 28, when the tap and power sensor both picked up signals, to test whether chips in the scheduled pool show training signatures despite the empty scheduler and to compare them with chips in the declared inference pool. The probe can classify the presented chips but cannot establish run identity.","action":"chip_probe","args":{"nodes":["B-0100","B-0350","B-0425","B-0500","B-0575","B-0625","B-0675","B-0725","B-0775","B-0800"],"hour":660}}
